title: Ham Crawford, Jack Gardner's orchestra and Wingy Manone
summary: Ham Crawford's background and the famous Jack Gardner orchestra; talk of Wingy Manone and the Doc Ross band.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel

blocks.x: Ham Crawford was actually from Tyler, Texas. I thought he had been. And, Dick, he had been playing with an orchestra in Dallas, which was very famous in those days, called the Jack Gardner Orchestra. And, so he'd been there a couple times to march to play with this other band. This goes very thankful. The Jack Gardner band was most popular in Texas, all of Texas, and they were in great demand. They rode the Pullman. They all wore the same beautiful suits. You know, not uniforms, but business suits. They traveled in great style. And, of course, kids, we'd go to the ballroom where they played, Holly's Hall. And, I have a good friend who managed to dance with me, let me know. So, I would get to hear them, and that's where I first heard him. But, he is famous for going around in different territories and getting bands, getting young guys who were good, and then taking them on the road.
I don't know how long Winging lasted, did he?
Well, Winging, yeah. Winging joined him in Albuquerque, New Mexico. And, well, no, I'm not so sure about that. Winging joined Doc Ross Band in Albuquerque.
I think there was some of those mix-ups there. But, I think, I believe I got this story from Jack, or from the book about Jack D.

Well, Winging is one of my oldest friends. And, we didn't play together until the thirties. But, we'd been friends. He had come through school for two or three times. And, after playing with him, that is how the original Buddy's Three Melody Boys came about. The Buddy's were part of him for the band. And, him decided he wanted to have a number two band. So, he got a job in Monroe. After he washed off his Daryl roof. The Washedaw Bank roof. That's where he was. One of the first roof columns and he was part of the country school. I can stop.
